Definition: from G1 (as a particle of union) and an obsolete νέπος (a brood); properly, akin, i.e. (specially) a cousin:--sister's son.
BiblicalUsage: Paul calls Mark his sister's son, his fellow worker, and tells the Colossians to receive him if he comes to them. The word is simply cousin, the nearest kin after brother and sister.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for cousin carries no doctrine of its own; its interest is the family tie, that Mark was Barnabas's cousin and Paul's fellow worker.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
